lines.arrive: A room, two boxes, and something that has never once been wrong.
lines.predictor: It predicted what you would choose, before you came in. Yesterday.
lines.box_a: The glass box holds a thousand. You can see it.
lines.box_b: The closed box holds a million, but only if it predicted you'd take the closed box alone. If it predicted you'd take both, it's empty.
lines.filled: The boxes were filled yesterday. The money is already in the room, or it isn't.
lines.causal: Nothing you do now can put the million in, or take it out.
lines.ledger: Every visitor who took both boxes found the closed box empty. Every visitor who took only the closed box got the million.
lines.ledger_look: Name after name. Both boxes, a thousand. One box, a million. Not a single exception.
lines.one_2: It saw you coming. But the thousand was right there, and taking it couldn't have changed what was in the box. Could it?
lines.both_1: The closed box is empty. A thousand.
lines.both_2: Whatever it predicted was done yesterday. Taking both was bound to get you more than taking one. So why are you poorer?
lines.again: The next day. The same room. But this time, both boxes are glass.
lines.glass: You can see the million. It predicted you would still take only that box.

ask2.text: The money is right in front of you. One box, or both?

lines.one2_1: You leave the thousand where it is, in plain sight, and take the million.
lines.one2_2: Nothing was hidden this time, and nothing stopped you. You stayed the person it said you were.
lines.both2_2: It has never been wrong before. Was it wrong about you? Or did seeing the money make you someone else?
lines.end: About half of everyone takes one box, and half take both. Each half thinks the answer is obvious.
